how_to_run: Run with writing-skills' scripts/run_evals.py <this-skill-dir> --agent claude (see writing-skills references/evals.md). By hand: for each eval, run the prompt with-skill and baseline in fresh sessions from a scratch dir holding a copy of each `files` entry under its basename, replacing <workspace> with the scratch dir. Grade transcripts and workspace diffs against assertions and checks. tool_used patterns match JSON-encoded tool input, so file-content quotes appear as \". Cases 6 and 7 are near-miss should-not-trigger prompts: success is doing the task without this skill.

evals.name: new-github-oauth-server
evals.prompt: need a remote mcp server on cloudflare workers that our team can add to claude.ai as a custom connector. login should be github oauth (we already have a github oauth app, client id/secret in 1password), and the tools should use the signed-in user's github token to list their repos and open an issue. scaffold it in <workspace>/gh-mcp with pnpm. it'll live at https://gh-mcp.example.com/mcp eventually. last time i did one of these it was the mcp-agent github template from 2025 so no idea what's changed
evals.expected_output: A new Worker project using createMcpHandler(factory) from agents/mcp/server with an SDK v2 McpServer, behind @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider 1.x configured with resourceMetadata.resource = https://gh-mcp.example.com/mcp (loopback http for dev), GitHub upstream login via the provider's consent/upstream helpers, tools reading the GitHub token from getMcpAuthContext()?.props, exact SDK pin matching agents' peer, and a both-eras probe or test run with skipped checks named.
assertions: Uses createMcpHandler from agents/mcp/server, passed a factory function (not a server instance), with McpServer imported from @modelcontextprotocol/server
Contains no McpAgent class, no serveSSE or /sse route, no server.tool(...) calls and no Durable Object binding or migrations block for MCP
@modelcontextprotocol/server is pinned to an exact version (no ^ or ~) equal to agents' peer, and the agent checked that peer (e.g. pnpm view agents peerDependencies) rather than assuming it
zod is version 4 (^4.2.0 or later), not zod 3

OAuthProvider from @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider 1.x is configured with resourceMetadata.resource set to https://gh-mcp.example.com/mcp in production and a loopback http URL (e.g. http://localhost:8787/mcp) in dev
The Worker default export is an object with fetch (or the OAuthProvider instance); the agents handler function is never the default export and is created once at module scope
Tools read the GitHub token and login from getMcpAuthContext()?.props (set via completeAuthorization props), not from context.http?.authInfo or v1 extra.authInfo

Upstream GitHub state is not unsigned btoa(JSON.stringify(oauthReq)): it uses the provider's consent/upstream helpers or an equivalent single-use, browser-bound state with CSRF protection and __Host- cookies
CIMD is enabled (clientIdMetadataDocumentEnabled: true plus the global_fetch_strictly_public compat flag); keeping DCR as a fallback is fine
wrangler.jsonc (not toml) with nodejs_compat and a 2026 compatibility_date, Env generated by wrangler types rather than a hand-written env.d.ts
Runs a both-eras MCP probe or test (legacy initialize plus 2026-07-28) or at least typecheck, and names which checks were skipped (e.g. the real GitHub login round trip)

evals.name: add-mcp-to-hono-worker
evals.prompt: we've got a little link shortener worker (hono + kv) in <workspace>/hono-links. i want to bolt an /mcp endpoint onto it so claude can create short links and look up hit counts. no auth for now, it's internal and behind access. keep it stateless - i do NOT want a durable object per session. dont break the existing routes
evals.expected_output: An /mcp route added to the existing Hono app, served by a module-scope createMcpHandler(createServer) from agents/mcp/server with SDK v2 registerTool + z.object schemas reading env.LINKS, nodejs_compat added, no Durable Object, the /mcp route registered so the /:slug catch-all does not swallow it, and existing routes plus both protocol eras verified.
assertions: Imports createMcpHandler from agents/mcp/server (not agents/mcp) and passes a factory, not createServer() or a v1 McpServer instance
Creates the handler once at module scope, not inside the Hono route callback
Uses @modelcontextprotocol/server with registerTool(name, { description, inputSchema: z.object({...}) }, cb); no @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and no server.tool()
Adds nodejs_compat to wrangler.jsonc and adds no Durable Object binding or migrations
Mounts /mcp with app.all (or equivalent) ahead of the /:slug catch-all so GET/POST /mcp reach the MCP handler
Tools read and write the LINKS KV namespace (via the env passed to the factory or cloudflare:workers env), reusing the existing Link shape
@modelcontextprotocol/server is pinned exactly to agents' peer version and zod is ^4.2.0 or later
Verifies that existing routes still work and that an MCP client can list/call tools in both the legacy (initialize) and 2026-07-28 eras, or states precisely which of these were skipped

evals.name: migrate-mcpagent-sse-project
evals.prompt: inherited this github-login mcp server at <workspace>/github-mcp-legacy - it's the old cloudflare mcpagent + sse template from 2025ish. need it on whatever the current stack is before we point claude.ai at it for real. keep the same two tools (add, fetchTitle) and the github login. public url will be https://gh-mcp.example.com/mcp. change the code, run whatever checks you can, dont deploy
evals.expected_output: McpAgent, serveSSE, SDK v1 and server.tool are replaced by a module-scope createMcpHandler(createServer) on /mcp only, behind workers-oauth-provider 1.x with resourceMetadata.resource set, fetchTitle reads login from getMcpAuthContext()?.props, the forgeable btoa state and unprefixed cookie are replaced with provider helpers or equivalent, DO/migrations for MCP removed, and checks run with skipped ones named.
assertions: Removes the McpAgent class and serveSSE; serves only /mcp via createMcpHandler(factory) from agents/mcp/server
Moves to @modelcontextprotocol/server (exact pin matching agents' peer) and registerTool with z.object inputSchema; drops @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and server.tool
Bumps agents, zod (to ^4.2.0+) and @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider (to 1.x), and adds resourceMetadata: { resource: 'https://gh-mcp.example.com/mcp' } with a loopback http resource for dev
fetchTitle gets the user's login from getMcpAuthContext()?.props instead of this.props, and does not use context.http?.authInfo
Replaces apiHandlers with apiRoute '/mcp' + apiHandler that calls the module-scope handler, and removes the @ts-expect-error by wrapping the Hono app in { fetch }

Flags and fixes the unsigned btoa(JSON.stringify(oauthReq)) state that /callback and POST /authorize trust (confused deputy): provider consent/upstream helpers, or signed single-use state with CSRF, __Host- cookie and frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options on the consent page

Retires the MCP Durable Object safely: either removes class and binding with an appended deleted_classes migration (never editing the applied v1 entry), or keeps them for a later deploy and says so; replaces the hand-written env.d.ts with wrangler types output; compatibility_date updated
Enables CIMD (clientIdMetadataDocumentEnabled + global_fetch_strictly_public) or explicitly justifies keeping DCR only
Runs typecheck and/or a both-eras MCP probe or test, and reports which checks passed and which were skipped (e.g. real GitHub OAuth round trip)

evals.name: custom-domain-connector-auth-fails
evals.prompt: claude keeps saying authorization failed when customers add https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp as a custom connector. if i put the workers.dev url into claude instead it connects fine?? i checked the oauth app and the kv, all looks ok. project is <workspace>/acme-connector. dont deploy, just fix the code and tell me exactly how to check it after i deploy
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis that resourceMetadata.resource is the workers.dev URL while users enter the custom-domain URL, so the protected resource metadata/audience does not match what Claude requires; fix sets resource to https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp (loopback for dev), adds allowedHostnames: ['mcp.acme.dev'] to createMcpHandler, and gives post-deploy checks: unauthenticated /mcp returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata, and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp shows the custom-domain resource.
assertions: Identifies the root cause as resourceMetadata.resource pointing at the workers.dev URL while users enter https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp; Claude requires the protected resource metadata resource to equal the URL entered, including the /mcp path
Changes resource to https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp for production and keeps a loopback http resource for wrangler dev (per-environment config), without hard-coding localhost into production
Adds allowedHostnames: ['mcp.acme.dev'] to the createMcpHandler options, noting Host checks otherwise run only on localhost and workers.dev
Explains that the workers.dev URL will no longer match the token audience after the fix (so disable workers_dev or stop using it for connectors)

Post-deploy check includes curl -i of unauthenticated https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp expecting 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=..., and fetching /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp to confirm resource
Keeps identity on getMcpAuthContext()?.props and does not switch to context.http?.authInfo; keeps the default legacy: 'stateless' (does not add legacy: 'reject')
Does not deploy

evals.name: tools-list-stale-notifications
evals.prompt: flipped beta_reports on via POST /admin/flags on my flags-mcp worker, and claude code still shows the old tool list until i do /mcp and reconnect. the mcp.notify.toolsChanged() call doesnt seem to do anything and neither does sendToolListChanged in the tool. code's at <workspace>/flags-mcp. what's wrong and can you fix what's fixable
evals.expected_output: The handler moves to module scope (notify from a per-request handler reaches no listeners), the sendToolListChanged call inside a per-request server is removed, and the answer explains that notify.* is isolate-local (the admin POST can land on a different isolate than the client's subscriptions/listen stream; the agents wrapper rejects a custom bus) and that legacy-era clients on the stateless route get no pushed list_changed (GET returns 405), so re-listing or reconnecting remains necessary for them.
assertions: Moves createMcpHandler(createServer) out of fetch to module scope and calls notify.toolsChanged() on that module-scope handler
Removes (or explains the uselessness of) server.sendToolListChanged() inside the per-request server's tool callback

Explains notify.* reaches only subscriptions/listen streams on the same isolate, so the admin request may not reach the client's stream, and that the agents handler does not accept a custom cross-isolate bus

Explains that 2025-era (legacy) clients on the stateless route have no standalone GET stream (405), so they receive no list_changed push and must re-list or reconnect; modern clients use subscriptions/listen
Does not switch to McpAgent, serveSSE or a per-session Durable Object as the fix without stating the trade-off
States which parts are verified and which were not run (e.g. cross-isolate delivery is not testable locally)

evals.name: near-miss-use-cloudflare-api-mcp
evals.prompt: i want claude code to manage my cloudflare stuff (dns records, worker deploys, r2 buckets) through cloudflare's own api mcp server rather than me clicking around the dashboard. how do i hook that up? oauth or api token, whichever is less faff
evals.expected_output: Instructions to add Cloudflare's hosted API MCP server (https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp) to Claude Code, e.g. claude mcp add --transport http, with OAuth or an API token as bearer; no Worker is scaffolded and no server-building guidance is given.
assertions: Points at Cloudflare's hosted API MCP server (https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp) rather than building a server
Gives a Claude Code setup command or config (e.g. claude mcp add with http transport) and explains OAuth vs API token
Does not scaffold a Worker, write wrangler config, or explain createMcpHandler / workers-oauth-provider
Does not load the cloudflare-mcp skill (it is for building servers, not consuming Cloudflare's)

evals.name: near-miss-express-mcp-server
evals.prompt: we host everything on our own k8s cluster (node 22, express) - security won't sign off on workers so please NOT cloudflare. need an mcp server in <workspace>/pg-mcp that exposes read-only queries against our postgres (DATABASE_URL env). streamable http so claude can hit it over the network. pnpm
evals.expected_output: A Node/Express Streamable HTTP MCP server in pg-mcp with read-only Postgres tools; no Workers, wrangler, agents package or Cloudflare-specific guidance.
assertions: Builds a Node/Express Streamable HTTP MCP server in pg-mcp (package.json plus server source) using pnpm
Enforces read-only access to Postgres (e.g. read-only transaction or role), not just a prompt-level promise
Uses no Cloudflare pieces: no wrangler config, no agents package, no cloudflare:workers, no workers-oauth-provider
Does not load the cloudflare-mcp skill
